statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-53493 (GO-2026-6597, GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645): containerd's image pull handlers walked the descriptors of an OCI image index without depth, breadth or deduplication limits, so pulling a crafted image can consume unbounded CPU and memory. OSV lists no affected symbols; the two fix commits the advisory names, 4f5f326 (Walk) and 94e83c1 (Dispatch) on the main branch, change only Walk and Dispatch in containerd's core/images package (handlers.go) and its test; on the release/2.3 branch the same changes are 03fbef3 and bfe1672, first released in v2.3.6. The fix ships in containerd 2.4.1, 2.3.6, 2.2.9, 2.0.13 and 1.7.36: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6597, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/4f5f32636d47f051751065cf824a10da70c619fe, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/94e83c14c8aac963e24e28105dab9c9af812a2a8, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/03fbef37dad145d03299b31a742023a7025e1c8a, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/bfe167214b9c17d48949aab74f213544a17464da . Read the Go build information and function table of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 91 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.30.0-r0, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0 (aarch64 only), every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. The only file in each package, and its only Go program, is the frontend program /usr/bin/build. It embeds github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 to v2.3.7, but the only containerd packages in their function tables (read from the Go line table, which also works on stripped binaries) are core/remotes/docker, core/remotes/docker/auth, core/remotes/errors, internal/lazyregexp, pkg/identifiers, pkg/reference and version (all under github.com/containerd/containerd/v2), and no build contains the containerd 1.x module. In every build, no core/images function, including Walk and Dispatch, is in any function table, and a byte search of each Go program, which would also catch inlined functions, finds no github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/core/images name, while the same searches find core/remotes/docker in every frontend program and runtime.main in every Go program. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search find core/images.Walk and core/images.Dispatch in containerd v2.2.7 (a vulnerable release) built from source for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the containerd version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-53493 (GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645, GO-2026-6597): containerd's image handlers walked a crafted OCI image index graph without depth, breadth or deduplication limits, so pulling a malicious image could consume unbounded CPU and memory. github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 is affected in 2.0.0 to 2.0.12, 2.1.0 to 2.2.8, 2.3.0 to 2.3.5 and 2.4.0, and fixed in 2.0.13, 2.2.9, 2.3.6 and 2.4.1. The fix bounds the traversal in core/images/handlers.go, in the Dispatch and Walk functions; on the release/2.3 branch these are commits bfe1672 (Dispatch) and 03fbef3 (Walk), first released in v2.3.6: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/bfe167214b9c17d48949aab74f213544a17464da, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/03fbef37dad145d03299b31a742023a7025e1c8a, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.6, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.1. Read every published docker-cli-buildx package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 0.33.0-r1 to the current 0.39.1-r1, 29 builds for aarch64 and 28 for x86_64 (0.34.1-r0 was published for aarch64 only), each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs one file, /usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx, a Go program: up to 0.39.0-r0 it is an executable dynamically linked against musl (its interpreter is /lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1 or /lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1 and its only needed library is the matching libc.musl shared object), and in 0.39.1-r0 and 0.39.1-r1 it is a statically linked executable built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information shows that builds before 0.37.2-r0 embed github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.2 to v2.3.4, inside the affected range, and that 0.37.2-r0 and every later build embed v2.3.6, v2.4.1 or v2.4.2; no build embeds v2.3.5 or v2.4.0. The Go function table (pclntab) of every build before 0.37.2-r0 contains github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/core/images.Dispatch and core/images.Walk, so the vulnerable functions are in the program. 0.37.2-r0 is the first fixed build for this owner.

CVE-2026-53493 (GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645, GO-2026-6597): before containerd 1.7.36, 2.0.13, 2.2.9, 2.3.6 and 2.4.1, the image handlers in core/images (Dispatch and Walk) traverse an OCI index without depth, breadth or deduplication limits, so pulling a crafted image index can consume unbounded CPU and memory. The fix bounds the traversal in core/images/handlers.go and adds the error "too many descriptors (limit %d)": https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6597, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/3e3b3daabc00cc7e467ebf22d4832966e7da9658 (in v2.3.6), https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.6. This owner covers the packages built from the Alpine docker recipe: docker, docker-engine, docker-cli and their support subpackages. Unpacked every subpackage of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 39 versions from 29.4.0-r1 to 29.10.0-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64 (29.4.3-r0 has no x86_64 docker-engine package), every download checked against the index checksum, and read the Go build information and function table (read with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every ELF file. The only ELF files are three Go programs: /usr/bin/dockerd and /usr/bin/docker-proxy in docker-engine, and /usr/bin/docker in docker-cli. The other subpackages contain no ELF files. runtime.main is found in the function table of every one of these programs, so the tables were read. /usr/bin/docker is built from the docker/cli vendor tree; only the 29.10.0-r1 builds record module versions in its build information. dockerd links the vulnerable handlers (core/images.Dispatch is in its function table in every build, and core/images.Walk in many). Its build information records containerd/v2 v2.2.2 to v2.3.5 in every build up to 29.8.1-r0, inside the affected range, and v2.3.6, v2.4.1 or v2.4.2 in every build from 29.8.2-r0 on; a string search finds the fix's error message in dockerd exactly from 29.8.2-r0. docker-proxy and /usr/bin/docker do not contain containerd: no containerd function is in either function table, the containerd/v2 module is absent from the build information of docker-proxy and of the 29.10.0-r1 /usr/bin/docker, and no docker/cli release in these builds vendors it (https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/v29.10.0/vendor/modules.txt). 29.8.2-r0 is the first build that carries the fix.

The other subpackages contain no ELF files. runtime.main is found in the function table of every one of these programs, so the tables were read. /usr/bin/docker is built from the docker/cli vendor tree; only the 29.10.0-r1 builds record module versions in its build information. dockerd links the vulnerable handlers (core/images.Dispatch is in its function table in every build, and core/images.Walk in many). Its build information records containerd/v2 v2.2.2 to v2.3.5 in every build up to 29.8.1-r0, inside the affected range, and v2.3.6, v2.4.1 or v2.4.2 in every build from 29.8.2-r0 on; a string search finds the fix's error message in dockerd exactly from 29.8.2-r0. docker-proxy and /usr/bin/docker do not contain containerd: no containerd function is in either function table, the containerd/v2 module is absent from the build information of docker-proxy and of the 29.10.0-r1 /usr/bin/docker, and no docker/cli release in these builds vendors it (https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/v29.10.0/vendor/modules.txt). 29.8.2-r0 is the first build that carries the fix.
